title: Ask and It Is Given: Learning to Manifest Your Desires
author: Esther Hicks and Jerry Hicks
target_audience: People interested in the Law of Attraction and manifestation
Those exploring alternative spirituality or Abraham-Hicks teachings
Readers looking for methods to improve happiness and well-being
core_themes: The Law of Attraction: like attracts like
The role of beliefs in shaping reality
Practical exercises to shift focus and energy
primary_purpose: To introduce readers to the philosophy of Abraham-Hicks and provide step-by-step guidance on using the Law of Attraction and emotional awareness to manifest desires, improve well-being, and consciously create a more fulfilling life.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational and channeled; driven by the voice of 'Abraham', a collective non-physical consciousness, as channeled by Esther Hicks.
structure_format.organization: Two main parts: (1) Theoretical teachings on the Law of Attraction and emotional guidance, and (2) 22 practical processes for manifesting desires and improving thought patterns.
features: Question and answer sections from workshops
Practices and processes for practical application

key_concepts_lessons: Your thoughts, emotions, and beliefs shape your reality.
Deliberate focus and positive emotion attract what you desire.
Emotions are a guidance system, indicating alignment with your desires.
Letting go of resistance and doubt is key to manifestation.
You always have control over your point of attraction.
Consistent, gentle improvement of thoughts can bring about desired changes.
notable_features: Introduction of Abraham-Hicks' Law of Attraction philosophy to a wide audience
22 practical manifestation processes, such as 'The Rampage of Appreciation' and 'The Focus Wheel'
Written largely in a channeled voice, creating a unique presentation style
Emphasizes emotional guidance and incremental progress
cultural_historical_context: Released at a time of revitalized interest in New Thought and the Law of Attraction, the book became part of a broader self-help and spiritual movement in the early 2000s. It helped pave the way for mainstream acceptance of manifesting principles, later popularized by works like 'The Secret'.
reception_impact: Widely influential in the Law of Attraction and spiritual self-help community
Praised for practical exercises and clarity
Criticized by skeptics for lack of scientific basis and reliance on channeled messages
Has inspired workshops, seminars, and a dedicated international following
Frequently cited as foundational reading for those interested in manifestation
comparable_titles: The Law of Attraction: The Basics of the Teachings of Abraham by Esther and Jerry Hicks
You Can Heal Your Life by Louise Hay
